what_it_is.prose: The Indian Air Force (IAF) is India's air arm under the Ministry of Defence and is the operator and customer of the country's military-airlift fleet that this Atlas tracks. Its transport backbone spans strategic heavy-lift — the Russian-origin Ilyushin Il-76MD 'Gajraj' (about 17 acquired 1985–89, flown by No. 25 Squadron, Chandigarh) and eleven US Boeing C-17 Globemaster III — medium and tactical lift via roughly 100+ Ukraine-origin Antonov An-32 (inducted from 1984) and Lockheed Martin C-130J-30 Super Hercules, and light transport such as the Dornier Do-228. The Il-76 airframe also underpins the IAF's Il-78MKI aerial-refuelling tankers and A-50EI 'Phalcon' AWACS. The IAF sustains these fleets through its Maintenance Command and Base Repair Depots — No. 1 BRD at Kanpur overhauls the An-32, while No. 3 BRD at Chandigarh handles Russian-origin transport and helicopter overhaul. Because the An-32 (Ukraine) and Il-76 (Russia) supply chains have been badly disrupted by the Russia-Ukraine war, the IAF has been driving indigenous overhaul, indigenised spares and digital-avionics life-extension to keep these fleets flying, while pursuing the Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) programme to eventually replace the An-32.

deployments_procurement.summary: The IAF operates a mixed strategic/tactical airlift fleet — Il-76 'Gajraj' and C-17 for heavy lift, An-32 and C-130J for tactical lift, Do-228 for light transport. It sustains these through its Base Repair Depots and is moving toward indigenous overhaul and life-extension of the Russian/Ukrainian-origin fleets, with the MTA programme intended to replace the An-32.

import_dependencies.summary: As operator, the IAF inherits the import dependencies of its foreign-origin fleets: Ukraine (Antonov airframe design authority, Ivchenko-Progress AI-20 engines for the An-32) and Russia (Ilyushin design authority, Aviadvigatel D-30KP engines for the Il-76), both disrupted by the Russia-Ukraine war, plus US OEM support for the C-17/C-130J.

items.note: Antonov / Ivchenko-Progress support disrupted by the war; driving indigenous overhaul at Kanpur BRD.
Ilyushin / Aviadvigatel support strained; PS-90 re-engine studied.
Boeing/Lockheed Martin FMS-based support for the US-origin airlifters.

faq.question: What transport aircraft does the Indian Air Force operate?
faq.answer: The IAF's airlift fleet spans strategic heavy-lift — about 17 Ilyushin Il-76MD 'Gajraj' (acquired 1985–89) and 11 Boeing C-17 Globemaster III — tactical/medium lift via roughly 100+ Antonov An-32 (from 1984) and Lockheed C-130J-30 Super Hercules, and light transport such as the Dornier Do-228. The Il-76 airframe also underpins the Il-78MKI tankers and A-50EI Phalcon AWACS.

faq.question: How does the IAF maintain its ageing Soviet/Russian-origin transport fleet?
faq.answer: The IAF sustains these fleets through its Maintenance Command Base Repair Depots — No. 1 BRD at Kanpur overhauls the An-32 and No. 3 BRD at Chandigarh handles Russian-origin transport and helicopter overhaul. With Russia/Ukraine supply chains disrupted by the war, the IAF has pushed indigenous overhaul, indigenised spares and digital-avionics life-extension, while pursuing the Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) programme to replace the An-32.
